model.name: R20.15: DRY-unify trace forward-key maps → single CHAIN_TYPE_CONFIG (eliminates BUG9-class by construction)
model.description: Today 5 PARALLEL forward-key maps must be kept in sync by hand — TraceModel.FORWARD_KEYS, server SCENARIO_FWD, server TRACE_FWD, server EXPECTED_CHILD_TYPE, and client forward-only.FORWARD_KEYS. A missing entry in any one (e.g. Bug) silently breaks /trace children (this was BUG9/BUG12). DURABLE FIX: collapse all 5 into ONE shared source of truth src/ts/shared/chain-model.ts `CHAIN_TYPE_CONFIG` + derived accessors; every consumer imports it. Adding a node type (Bug/ChangeRequest/etc.) is then a single-place edit, eliminating the BUG9-class of defects BY CONSTRUCTION. Parity-regression AC: the unified config must produce IDENTICAL forward keys to the old 5 maps for every existing type. Ships AFTER the BUG9 stopgap (v0.6.31).
model.tronQuote: > Architect design (PO-accepted): 5 maps → 1 CHAIN_TYPE_CONFIG, all consumers import.
model.crossRefNote: DURABLE fix for the BUG9 (6da84135) / BUG12 (merged) root cause — the forward-key map drift. BUG9 is the stopgap (add Bug entries to the 5 maps, v0.6.31); R20.15 unifies them so the class of defect cannot recur. DEPENDENCY: R20.15 ships AFTER the BUG9 stopgap v0.6.31. R20.4 (ea212274, Bug+ChangeRequest extend Requirement) is the OOP rationale the unified config encodes.

intendedChain.useCase: chainModel.unifiedForwardKeys — single CHAIN_TYPE_CONFIG drives forward keys + expected child types for every node type; all consumers derive from it
intendedChain.method: getForwardKeys(type) / getExpectedChildTypes(type) — derived accessors replacing the 5 hand-synced maps
intendedChain.test: PARITY: for every existing node type, unified config == old 5 maps (SCENARIO_FWD, TRACE_FWD, EXPECTED_CHILD_TYPE, TraceModel.FORWARD_KEYS, client forward-only.FORWARD_KEYS). RED before refactor proves equivalence target; GREEN after.
